teja: quick q — when calling Redwood from a client inside a customer's VPC+proxy, should we set REDWOOD_BASE_URL to the private endpoint, or keep api.redwood.com and rely on the proxy to rewrite Host headers? I'm seeing intermittent auth 401s in the Java client.

sam: my short recommendation: set the base_url to the private endpoint if you control the client runtime. Host-rewrite is fragile, esp with HTTP/2 multiplexing and mTLS in the path. Use host-rewrite only as a last-resort fallback.

lina: +1. Also check the token audience (aud). We had a case where the access token was minted for api.redwood.com but the proxy forwarded to private.redwood.corp => 401 from our side.

mike: example env we standardize on for private deployments: 
```
REDWOOD_BASE_URL=https://private.redwood.example
REDWOOD_AUTH_AUDIENCE=private.redwood.example
REDWOOD_USE_MTLS=true
REDWOOD_CLIENT_TIMEOUT_MS=60000
```
This fixed the auth and TLS issues for Node + Python SDKs.

teja: thanks — I'm on the Java client. Any streaming-specific quirks to watch for (long polling / streaming responses)?

sam: streaming notes: proxies that aggressively idle/close idle HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 streams can chop chunked responses. Two practical fixes: (1) tune proxy keepalive/read-idle thresholds, (2) enable client-side reconnect + resume logic + small heartbeat frames. For Java, we added an exponential backoff with jitter and a short prefix-cache replay for the last 1-2 tokens. Also consider setting `Connection: keep-alive` and disabling `http2` downgrade if proxy mishandles HPACK.

lina: don't forget SNI — if the proxy doesn't forward SNI the TLS handshake might pick the wrong cert for the private host. That again looks like a 401/handshake failure depending on client.

infra-bot: deploy-check: java-sdk-integration (staging) reproduced 401 on streaming smoke test at 2024-11-03T15:12:33Z — attaching logs to the ticket.

teja: log excerpt looked like: 
```
WARN okhttp3.internal.http2.Http2Connection - stream was reset: CANCEL
java.io.IOException: unexpected end of stream
...
401 Unauthorized: audience mismatch: expected=private.redwood.example got=api.redwood.com
```

mike: if you can't change the client's base_url, you can also retry on 401 once after refreshing token with aud override (not ideal, but worked when changing config wasn't possible). Just be careful not to loop refresh.
